notes:
• Resume, continue or fork your Claude Code and Codex sessions: /claude resume and /codex resume list them, in this folder or all of them.
• Main answers a Claude Code or Codex pane once the work on its message is done, and the pane sets how many answers come without you.
• Close a desktop tab with its ×, a middle-click, its menu or ⌥⌘W, and you're asked first if closing it would stop work running in it.
• File tools and patches stay in the folders your permission profile allows: a path sent as a list can no longer skip the folder rules.
changes: Main answers an agent's message once it has finished, with its answer.
Two messages typed into a Claude Code or Codex pane in a row arrive as two.
What ZTC types into a Claude Code or Codex pane carries no control characters.
Main's messages carry the name its pane goes by.
Closing a prompt that opened in Main by itself says what it closed.
A line ZTC shows only in this terminal stays out of the turn's recap.
/help shows every command as you type it.
A Router key that is stored broken, or that its provider refused, says so in Router's words.
A request Zerg Router fails says what failed, with its HTTP status.
A session whose diagnostics were masked differently between checkpoints loads again.
Resume your Claude Code and Codex sessions.
/claude -- TEXT and /codex -- TEXT start a fresh session with the text as its prompt, word for word
The pane that starts an exchange with Main chooses how long Main answers it by itself.
Close a tab in the desktop app.
The desktop app's mirror answers only the link ZTC gives.
A pane's own credential no longer types as you, or into a shell or a command pane.
A message for a ZTC pane that is still starting waits for it, and is never typed in.
The pane relay forwards only what a pane may send.
On Linux the pane relay's socket is yours alone.
apply_patch reads a diff's names exactly as git does, NUL bytes and all.
A confined write cannot build a new git directory.
A path or patch must be well-formed Unicode text.
apply_patch writes only where a permission profile allows.
git no longer runs a command a confined agent planted.
apply_patch no longer shows a file outside the root through a link it made.
A Codex apply_patch heredoc is a file write.
A denied path is denied however it's spelled.
A file tool reads only a path the profile checked.
